job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

passage: Today in our science lab, we examined various plants to understand their hidden functions. First, we carefully pulled up a grass plant and a carrot. We observed that the grass has many thin, branching roots, while the carrot has one thick, central root. This shows that root systems vary significantly between different species. Next, we looked at a hibiscus flower. We removed the colorful petals and discovered the stamens and pistil inside, which are essential reproductive organs. A flower remains a flower even without its showy petals. We then placed a leafy twig in a beaker of water under sunlight. We noticed tiny water droplets forming inside a plastic bag tied over the leaves. This process, called transpiration, is how plants release excess water vapor into the air, not a way to cool down like human sweating. Finally, we dug up a potato and found it growing underground, yet it is actually a stem, not a root, because it has buds that can grow into new shoots. These observations prove that plant parts have specific roles beyond just holding the plant or looking pretty. Understanding these structures helps us see how plants survive and grow in their environments.

items.evidence: We noticed tiny water droplets forming inside a plastic bag tied over the leaves.
items.q: Droplets collect inside a bag tied over leaves. What do they show the leaves did?
options: Let out extra water as vapour
Took in water from the air
items.explain: The droplets come from water vapour the leaves released, which is transpiration.

wrong.why: reverses the direction of water movement
thinks sunlight is a material plants use
thinks transpiration is sweating to cool down

items.q: How is transpiration in plants different from sweating in humans?
options: It removes extra water, not heat
It removes extra heat, not water
It happens only when roots are cut
It happens only in the dark
items.explain: Transpiration releases excess water vapor; it is not a way to cool down like sweating.

items.q: A potato grows underground. Why is it still called a stem?

Its skin is thick and brown
It stores food for the plant

items.explain: A potato has buds that can grow into new shoots, so it is a stem even underground.

It is no longer a flower at all
